clue.text: Observation's not about to evaluate work

indicators.note: not says the following word's letters are to be left out of the observation

parts.note: an observation is a remark, a passing comment
re is Latin-derived shorthand for about or concerning

explanation.surface: A comment that has nothing to say about how to assess someone's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes RE (about) away from REMARK.
explanation.definitionFit: Teachers assess homework by grading it, a common sense of the verb.

clue.text: Trapped criminal needs guards worked up

indicators.note: guards says the first part surrounds and protects the second
criminal suggests something crooked or bent out of shape, so the letters of needs are rearranged
in a down clue, up says the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to work a machine is to run it; ran is the past tense

explanation.surface: A cornered crook requires watchmen who are agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges the letters to ENSED, which goes round NAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone caught in a snare or net has been trapped: direct synonym.

clue.text: Magistrate abandoning rate reforms in disgrace

indicators.note: abandoning says the letters of rate are left behind from the magistrate
reforms says the remaining letters are shaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A magistrate gives up on rate reforms and falls into disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' removes RATE from MAGISTRATE, leaving MAGIST; 'reforms' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark of shame or disgrace attached to someone is a synonym in this sense.

clue.text: Dark version of Crimson Tide rejected without it being completely abandoned

parts.note: maroon is a deep brownish crimson

indicators.note: without says the letters of it are taken away from the turned-round tide
rejected says the word tide is thrown back, read in reverse

explanation.surface: A darker shade of Crimson Tide (the Alabama football team) turned down without it being fully dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns TIDE into EDIT; 'without' takes IT away, leaving ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stranded alone on an island, left with no help, is the classic sense.

clue.text: Training about education lifting writer's block

indicators.note: lifting says the writer's piece is raised to the top of this down entry

parts.note: the writer's is I'm, the setter speaking of themself

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: PE is physical education, training in the gym

explanation.surface: A course to help an author overcome writer's block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's' means I'M, the setter's own voice; in a down entry 'lifting' raises that piece to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: To obstruct or hinder progress is to block it: verb synonym.

clue.text: Force original sinner to turn religious fanatic

parts.note: torque is a twisting force

indicators.note: to turn says the sinner's name is read backwards

parts.note: Adam committed the first sin in Genesis

explanation.surface: Make the first sinner repent and become a zealot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' makes ADAM into MADA. Tomás de Torquemada led the Spanish Inquisition.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquemada, the notorious Grand Inquisitor, stands as the type of a zealous persecutor.

clue.text: Present sociology's case for unorthodox view

parts.note: to be present is to be here

indicators.note: case means the outer letters, the shell around the word sociology

explanation.surface: Arguing the case for a radical idea in sociology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' picks the outside letters S and Y of 'sociology'.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is a belief contrary to accepted doctrine, an unorthodox opinion.

clue.text: Wind up in care for backing police search

indicators.note: in says the teasing word sits inside the other piece
backing says the word is run in reverse

parts.note: to care for is to tend
to wind someone up is to tease them, to rag them

explanation.surface: Getting irritated in a care home because of supporting someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind up' looks like the definition but is the tease piece; 'backing' turns the care word round to DNET.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragnet is a systematic sweep by police to catch suspects.

clue.text: Corrupt landlords leaving North Dakota for American capital

indicators.note: corrupt suggests something debased, so the letters are rearranged
leaving says the state's letters depart from the landlords

parts.note: ND is the postal abbreviation of North Dakota

explanation.surface: Dishonest property owners quit North Dakota to make money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes ND out of LANDLORDS, leaving LALORDS; 'Corrupt' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: US currency is money, and capital in the financial sense means funds.

clue.text: Member's entrance to Jersey?

parts.note: a member is a limb, and a jersey here is a pullover, not the Channel Island; the opening in it for the arm

explanation.surface: How a politician might be admitted to the island of Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey wants to be the Channel Island; it is the knitted garment.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening in a garment where the sleeve joins and a limb goes through.

clue.text: Compare some internecine killing with revolution

indicators.note: with revolution says the portion is turned round, read backwards
some says only a portion of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Likening some internal killing to a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes NEKIL across 'interneciNE KILling'; 'with revolution' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a likeness between two things is to compare them: verb synonym.

clue.text: Bizarre attempt to accept request initially, upsetting the balance

indicators.note: to accept says the attempt takes another letter inside it

parts.note: to have a go is to make an attempt

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of request
upsetting says the leftover letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the balance is the rest of the word request once its first letter has gone

explanation.surface: A strange effort to take on a request that disturbs the equilibrium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the balance' means what is left of 'request' after its first letter; 'upsetting' rearranges that into TESQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grotesque is weirdly distorted or outlandish: adjective synonym.

clue.text: Apply particular programme to oust leader

parts.note: an app is a computer programme

indicators.note: to oust leader says the first letter is pushed out

parts.note: certain, as in certain people, means particular

explanation.surface: Use a specific program to remove the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to oust leader' drops C from CERTAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To pertain or relate to something is to apply to it: formal verb synonym.

clue.text: Decorator is not commonly wearing lead belt

indicators.note: wearing says the metal piece has the other around it like clothing

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
ain't is the colloquial form of is not
to belt is to go very fast, to rush

explanation.surface: A decorator, speaking colloquially, isn't wearing a lead-weighted belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' marks the dialect contraction of 'is not'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool that decorates walls stands in for a decorator: the thing that does the decorating.

clue.text: Rival reported leading articles in New Musical Express

indicators.note: reported says the letters are spoken, as a reporter would
leading articles plays on the newspaper term; here the opening letters of each word

explanation.surface: A rival publication's coverage in the lead stories of the NME music paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading articles in' takes N, M, E, the NME music paper's initials; spoken as letters they are 'en-em-ee'.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent or adversary in a contest is a rival: noun synonym.

clue.text: Lost control of business finally getting wound up

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of business

parts.note: to wind someone up is to tease or kid them

explanation.surface: A firm finally collapses, going into liquidation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the last letter S of 'business'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle that slides out of the driver's grip has skidded, losing control.

clue.text: This colours audience's perception of Stamp's hard man

indicators.note: what an audience perceives is what it hears

parts.note: a die is a stamp for coins, and a tough is a hard man, so 'die's tough'

explanation.surface: How viewers see Terence Stamp's tough-guy screen character.
explanation.walkthrough: Stamp wants to be the actor Terence Stamp; it is a die, the tool that stamps coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance used for dyeing is something that colours: 'this' stands for the answer.

clue.text: Took a step backwards to hold husband showing no signs of life

indicators.note: to hold says the reversed word surrounds the other piece
backwards says the step word is read in reverse

parts.note: trod is the past tense of tread, to take a step
a husband is a woman's man

explanation.surface: Someone retreated to cradle a husband who appeared to be dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' turns the step word round to DORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means inactive or sleeping, as a seed or volcano shows no activity.

clue.text: Drops popular artist before season in New York

indicators.note: before says the first pieces come ahead of the season

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
in means fashionable, popular
Americans call autumn fall

explanation.surface: A well-liked painter quits ahead of autumn in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain arrives as drops, so a fall of rain is drops collectively; noun sense.

clue.text: Tense cast regularly seen in this place

definitions.text: Tense cast regularly seen in this place

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: seen in says the picked letters appear inside the other piece

parts.note: this place is here

indicators.note: regularly picks alternate letters of the word cast

explanation.surface: A nervous company of actors is regularly found at this venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes alternate letters of 'cast'; the whole clue also describes the place where a cast performs.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is where a nervous cast of actors performs regularly, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Abandon area of London east of The Strand

indicators.note: east of says only what lies to the right of the shore piece is kept

parts.note: Shoreditch is a district of east London
a strand is a shore or beach

explanation.surface: Leave a London district for somewhere east of the Strand, the famous London street.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand wants to be the London street; it is a beach. Shoreditch is an area of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is to get rid of it or abandon it: informal verb synonym.

clue.text: Failing double agents might do this

definitions.meaning: a failing is a flaw or shortcoming
to switch sides to the enemy, as turncoat spies do

explanation.definitionFit: A flaw is a defect as a noun; a spy who changes allegiance defects as a verb.

clue.text: Ring dove periodically ignored bird

parts.note: a hoop is a ring

indicators.note: periodically ignored says every other letter of dove is skipped

explanation.surface: A ringed dove was now and then overlooked by a birdwatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically ignored' drops D and V, keeping OE.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoopoe is a crested bird with a distinctive call, a specific example of a bird.

clue.text: Get out of former home, evicted from complex

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: evicted from says the home piece is thrown out of the other

parts.note: intricate means complex
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Leaving one's old house after being turfed out of an apartment block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evicted from' removes IN from INTRICATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To extricate oneself is to free oneself from a difficulty, to escape.

clue.text: Hard nuts climbing naked here? Probably not!

indicators.note: climbing says the stripped letters are read upwards in this down entry
naked says the words hard nuts are stripped bare, exposing the letters inside them

explanation.surface: Tough guys going naked in the Arctic plain? Unlikely!
explanation.walkthrough: The draft had no indicator for the concealed letters; 'naked' exposes ARDNUT inside 'Hard nuts', and also feeds the surface's joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen Arctic plain is no place to strip off, a whimsical description of the place.

clue.text: Give up after tax returns overlooked

parts.note: to forgo is to give up

indicators.note: returns says the word is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: nett income is what is left after tax

explanation.surface: Abandon something once the tax forms are filed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns NETT into TTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overlooked has slipped the mind: past participle synonym.

clue.text: Row as leader of boat crew steps forward

indicators.note: as leader of says the change happens at the front of the crew word
steps says a new letter steps into that place

parts.note: a rowing eight is a boat crew
F is short for forward

explanation.surface: A rowing crew's stroke moves up the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as leader of' and 'steps' replace the first letter E of EIGHT with F.
explanation.definitionFit: A row, rhyming with cow, is a quarrel or fight.

clue.text: Objective bird has a change of heart

indicators.note: has a change of heart says the middle letters are switched round

parts.note: bird is British slang for prison time, so a jail or gaol

explanation.surface: An aim for a bird that changes its mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Doing bird is British slang for serving a prison sentence; GAOL is the British spelling of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: An objective is an aim, a target to reach: noun synonym.

clue.text: Rejected players no longer available

parts.note: the players in a production are the cast
a dish no longer available on a menu is off

explanation.surface: Turned-down actors are not on offer any more.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes discarded by one owner are cast-offs, things thrown aside.

clue.text: Rent out again for free

definitions.meaning: to let a property once more on a new lease
to let go or set loose

explanation.definitionFit: Letting a property again on a new lease is one sense; setting someone loose is the other.
